newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were down at midday on Thursday on weak market sentiment worsened by consecutive falls of the market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
The index fell 0.401 point or 0.81 percent to 48.987 points, on volume of 2.2 million shares worth $959,000. Of 41 B shares, 28 traded, with 12 down, eight flat and eight up.
Brokers said that Shanghai Lujiazui's fall depressed market sentiment and pushed the index down.
Lujiazui traded the most, dropping $0.020 or 2.27 percent to $0.860 on volume of 442,200 shares.
"Falls in Pudong shares indicated that domestic investors are staying on the sidelines waiting for a better chance," one broker said.
"The index will fall further in the short term until the exchange denies the rumours that domestic investors will be restrained from trading B shares," he added.
"It is likely to test the 48 point support level this afternoon," a second trader said.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation was the biggest loser, falling $0.006 or 4.28 percent to $0.134 on volume of 178,000 shares.
Shanghai A shares were up on a technical rebound after sharp losses on Wednesday, but the upside potential would be limited, brokers said.
The A index rose 3.643 points or 0.46 percent to 798.901 points, on volume of 86.0 million shares worth 727.2 million yuan. The SSE 30 rose 15.032 points or 0.74 percent to 2046.975 points.
Xinjiang Zhonghe was the star, jumping 0.74 yuan or 8.32 percent to 9.63 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
